verdicts.claim: Latest stable PostgreSQL is 18.6 (2026-08-13); PostgreSQL 19 Beta 3 released 2026-08-13
verdicts.note: Homepage news item dated August 13, 2026: 'PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, 14.24 and 19 Beta 3 Released!' (28 security fixes).

All three dates and support strings are on the news page verbatim (3.6.0 says 'PostgreSQL 12 - 18beta3'). HOWEVER the research summary's framing that 3.6.1 is 'current stable' is wrong: postgis.net/source lists postgis-3.6.4.tar.gz as current; GitHub tags show 3.6.2 (2026-02-09), 3.6.3 (2026-04-14), 3.6.4 (2026-06-08) and 3.5.7 (2026-06-10). The news page hides these under generic 'PostGIS Patch Releases' titles (Feb 9 and Apr 14, 2026). 3.6.2/3.6.3 NEWS entries still say 'requires PostgreSQL 12-18'.

verdicts.claim: PG 18 released 2025-09-25 with async I/O (io_method worker/io_uring/sync), skip scan, uuidv7(), virtual generated columns, OLD/NEW in RETURNING, statistics preserved by pg_upgrade, checksums default on, OAuth auth, md5 deprecated, protocol 3.2
verdicts.note: Release date September 25, 2025; every listed feature appears in the announcement, including 'io_method ... worker and io_uring ... sync', 'skip scan', uuidv7(), virtual generated columns, OLD/NEW in RETURNING, planner statistics kept through major upgrade, checksums on by default in initdb, oauth authentication, md5 deprecation, wire protocol 3.2.

Table matches exactly: 18 (18.6) final release November 14, 2030; 17 (17.11) November 8, 2029; 16 (16.15) November 9, 2028; 15 (15.19) November 11, 2027; 14 (14.24) November 12, 2026. 13 went EOL November 13, 2025.

verdicts.claim: Planner handles 'up to a few thousand partitions fairly well' with pruning; more remaining partitions after pruning -> longer planning and higher memory; 'Never just assume that more partitions are better than fewer partitions, nor vice-versa'
verdicts.note: PostgreSQL 18.6 docs, section 5.12.6 'Best Practices for Declarative Partitioning': all three sentences present verbatim, including the 'provided that typical queries allow the query planner to prune all but a small number of partitions' qualifier.

verdicts.claim: Edition feature split: hypertables/create_hypertable/show_chunks/drop_chunks in both; columnstore/hypercore, continuous aggregates, retention policies, add_job/alter_job, reorder/move/split chunk are Community (TSL) only; 'You cannot sell TimescaleDB Community Edition as a service'
verdicts.note: Feature table: create_hypertable/show_chunks/drop_chunks in both editions; reorder_chunk/move_chunk/split_chunk, all columnstore/hypercore functions, all continuous-aggregate functions, add_retention_policy, add_job/alter_job/delete_job/run_job are Community-only. Quote present: 'You cannot sell TimescaleDB Community Edition as a service, even if you are the main contributor.' The page names the license TSL.

verdicts.claim: TimescaleDB 2.29.2 released 2026-08-18; supports PostgreSQL 16, 17, 18; 'PostgreSQL 15 Support Removed' in 2.29.0
verdicts.note: Releases: 2.29.2 (Aug 18, 2026), 2.29.1 (Aug 4), 2.29.0 (Jul 28). The 2.29.0 notes say 'Important: PostgreSQL 15 Support Removed ... This release supports PostgreSQL 16, 17, and 18.' The 2.29.2 notes themselves do not restate the PG range; cite 2.29.0 for it.

verdicts.claim: pg_partman: time- and number-based partition sets, 'PostgreSQL >= 14', 'only built-in, declarative partitioning is supported', includes 'A background worker (BGW) process ... to automatically run partition maintenance without the need of an external scheduler', retention via dropping old partitions
verdicts.note: README: 'PostgreSQL >= 14'; 'As of version 5.0.1, only built-in, declarative partitioning is supported and the older trigger-based methods have been deprecated'; BGW 'to automatically run partition maintenance without the need of an external scheduler (cron, etc) in most cases'; 'both time-based and number-based table partition sets'; 'dropping old ones based on a retention policy'.

verdicts.claim: pg_partman latest tag v5.5.0 published 2026-07-22T14:46:50Z; BGW role default changed to partman_maintainer; CVE fixes for SQL injection/privilege escalation; detach-before-drop support; RLS maintenance_role
verdicts.note: tag_name v5.5.0, published_at 2026-07-22T14:46:50Z. Body: pg_partman_bgw.role now defaults to partman_maintainer (breaking); CVE-2026-61781/61817/61818 (SQL injection + privilege escalation in time encoder/decoder), CVE-2026-61819 (pg_jobmon), CVE-2026-61820 (template-table privilege escalation), CVE-2026-61821 (ownership takeover), CVE-2026-61822; new detach_before_drop flag; maintenance_role column for RLS on config tables.

corrections: PostGIS: replace every 'PostGIS 3.6.1 is current stable' statement. Current stable is PostGIS 3.6.4 (2026-06-08); 3.6.2 (2026-02-09) and 3.6.3 (2026-04-14) also shipped, and 3.5.7 (2026-06-10) is the latest 3.5.x. Source: https://postgis.net/source/ (lists postgis-3.6.4.tar.gz) and https://github.com/postgis/postgis/tags. The 3.6.x line still requires PostgreSQL 12-18 (3.6.2/3.6.3 NEWS). The /news/ page hides patch releases under generic 'PostGIS Patch Releases' titles, so cite /source/ or the tags page for 'latest'.

Open question closed (PostGIS Docker tags): postgis/postgis:18-3.6 and postgis/postgis:18-3.6-alpine exist on Docker Hub (pushed within the last ~2 weeks, linux/amd64) and are listed in the docker-postgis README; 19beta1-3.6 and 19beta1-3.6-alpine also exist; there is no 18-3.7 tag yet. Operational gotcha from the README: for PostgreSQL 18+ images the default VOLUME path changed to /var/lib/postgresql (earlier images used /var/lib/postgresql/data) - fix compose volume mounts and any testcontainers fixture that binds the data directory.

Open question closed (Garage S3 feature gaps): the S3 compatibility page (https://garagehq.deuxfleurs.fr/documentation/reference-manual/s3-compatibility/, last updated 2022-05-25) still says 'Garage does not (yet) support object versioning', all Bucket/Object Tagging endpoints are 'Missing', all Object Lock / legal hold / retention endpoints are 'Missing', and lifecycle supports only AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload and Expiration. The v2.3.0 release notes (2026-04-16, https://git.deuxfleurs.fr/Deuxfleurs/garage/releases/tag/v2.3.0) add none of these (only a LifecycleWorker bug fix), so the no-versioning/no-tagging gap stands; cite both pages and note the compat page's age. Also update the dev-ergonomics comparison: Garage v2.3.0 added 'garage server --single-node' plus env-var auto-creation of an access key and bucket, which is comparable to SeaweedFS 'weed mini'.

Open question closed (managed TimescaleDB): Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server ships only the Apache-2 edition - Microsoft moderator (2023-10-11): 'We only support free version of timescale under apache license. Community version is under proprietary TSL ... We have no plans to support proprietary licensed extensions' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1380687/). Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL does not list timescaledb at all in its supported-extensions table (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-extensions.html), while it does ship pg_partman and PostGIS for PG 18. Conclusion for the ADR: on the major managed hosts the TSL features (columnstore, continuous aggregates, retention policies, jobs) are unavailable, so the native-partitioning + pg_partman decision is effectively locked in unless self-hosting or using Tiger Cloud.

pg_partman version drift on managed hosts: RDS PostgreSQL 18.4 ships pg_partman 5.4.3 (not 5.5.0) and PostGIS 3.6.3. Do not make the ADR depend on 5.5.0-only features (detach_before_drop, maintenance_role RLS) if RDS is a target; state the minimum pg_partman version explicitly.

pg_partman 5.5.0 breaking change must be reflected in the bootstrap: pg_partman_bgw.role now defaults to partman_maintainer, so the role must be created with the right privileges (or the GUC set) or the BGW will not run maintenance; retention target schemas must be owned by the same role as the child tables. Add both to the operational notes.

Open question partly closed (PgBouncer interplay, from https://www.pgbouncer.org/features.html): in transaction pooling mode LISTEN is 'Never' supported, SET/RESET 'Never', PREPARE/DEALLOCATE 'Never'; protocol-level prepared statements work only with max_prepared_statements set non-zero. Consequence: Procrastinate/PgQueuer workers (LISTEN/NOTIFY) need a direct connection or a session-mode pool; asyncpg/psycopg 3 behind a transaction-mode PgBouncer need max_prepared_statements > 0 or client-side statement caching disabled (asyncpg statement_cache_size=0, psycopg prepare_threshold=None).

TimescaleDB citation precision: the 'supports PostgreSQL 16, 17, and 18' sentence appears in the 2.29.0 release notes, not in the 2.29.2 notes; cite 2.29.0 for the PG range and 2.29.2 only for the date.
PostGIS 3.6.0 citation precision: the 3.6.0 announcement says 'PostgreSQL 12 - 18beta3'; PG 18 GA support in the 3.6 line is first stated at 3.6.1. Do not cite 3.6.0 as evidence of PG 18 GA support.
